claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model should be certified for release based on aggregate launch readiness and general governance guidance, despite an unresolved evaluation gap in the disability accommodations intake segment and an open legal question about whether that gap must be disclosed under policy.
decision_criteria: Use 'compliant' only if admissible evidence shows certification satisfies both aggregate readiness and the policy requirement for the named use-case gap.
Use 'suspicious' if aggregate readiness is supported but a required support link for disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance is missing.
Use 'noncompliant' if admissible evidence shows certification proceeded in contradiction to policy or with no plausible basis at all.
General public governance guidance can support monitoring/documentation posture, but it cannot cure a missing internal policy predicate.
evidence_requests: Evidence that the material limitation will be disclosed before launch, if certification is to proceed.
Evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this named segment before launch, if disclosure will not occur.
Final legal determination on whether the disability accommodations intake gap must be disclosed.
Any release-governance record showing certification is allowed to proceed while this policy question remains unresolved.
specific_concerns: Aggregate readiness evidence does not resolve the separate policy predicate for a named launch use case with a known gap.
The affected segment is named in two university accommodation commitments, which weighs toward materiality under the provided policy text.
The policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Legal review is still open, so the disclosure predicate is unresolved on the current record.
The Product 'non-core' characterization based on 5% projected traffic is expressly insufficient to resolve materiality when customer commitments or pending legal review exist.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record without showing either disclosure, resolution of the gap, or approved risk acceptance.
That the affected segment is immaterial based on low projected traffic alone.
Any implication that general model-card or AI risk-management guidance substitutes for the specific internal disclosure requirement.
